compute: GPU 3, fold-4 pilot ~1.6 h (3 teacher inferences on 7150 rows, student 3000 updates, eval)
question: Does self-training on consensus pseudo-points (>= 3 of 4 fold-clean detectors agree within 8 px on the fold's own training rows) improve held-out localisation and the hex6 HEX signal of a single detector beyond what seed averaging gives?
prior: st1 (single confident teacher): F1 +0.024, no downstream change. Detector ensembling raised the HEX gain 2.5x, so detection noise matters; a consensus teacher is a much cleaner label source than one teacher.
teachers: stride-2 s46, s47, s48 (single-view peaks >= 0.2 on training rows)

pseudo_labels.positives: mean position of >= 3 agreeing teachers (8 px), Gaussian sigma 8 targets at stride 2
pseudo_labels.negatives: stride-2 cells > 16 px from every teacher peak at threshold 0.2

student: stride-2 head on the fold-4 recipe A encoder; batch = 1 strong (train-green 20 x 4 flips, ROI-masked) + 1 pseudo item; 3000 updates; AdamW 1e-5 / 1e-3; seed 46
evaluation: val-5 F1 at 0.35 vs the seed-46 stride-2 detector (0.666); calibration-free r(log hex6_all, log HEX) and error correlation on the 1790 fold-4 validation rows, student vs seed-46
pre_specified_decision: extend to five folds (then LOFO on A and B, alone and inside the 13-detector ensemble) only if val-5 F1 >= 0.70 and the student's hex6 r exceeds the seed-46 detector's; otherwise close self-training on this track
falsification: F1 < 0.70 or no hex6 correlation gain means the consensus teacher only re-teaches what the seeds already agree on.
